description: Driven by a genuine curiosity for lunar exploration, we aim to push the boundaries of what's possible in space tech. By combining software engineering, advanced simulation, and creative problem-solving, our team designs intuitive, intelligent solutions to tackle the complex challenges of lunar orbit missions.
summary: TARS compares landing sites across dates to find the most usable mission window. One view shows sunlight, mission risk and communication conditions, and you can switch between 3, 7 and 14 day missions. On the 3D surface, you can watch the Sun and Earth move relative to the horizon while power and communication windows are analyzed. Elevation, slope and roughness maps for every site point to safer landing spots. Results rest on NASA LOLA terrain data and are checked against JPL Horizons. Every analysis carries a model confidence score, so its limits stay clear. Planners, educators and the public can understand lunar mission data and decide quickly.
details:
TARS - Terrain analysis & Reconnaissance System

How It Works

Our project analyzes and compares potential landing sites at the lunar South Pole. It details each site's slope, roughness, surrounding terrain relief, Sun and Earth visibility, and communication conditions. Once a user selects a site, they can view the 3D terrain, horizon visibility, and mission based analysis. If the launch date, mission duration, or priorities change, the tool also calculates the best time window.

As data, we used NASA LOLA's south polar DEM (Digital Elevation Model), site locations, and Sun & Earth position data. We calculate and present these through charts and visuals so that users can easily see at a glance whether a site has an excessive slope, how long solar illumination is available, and what the communication conditions with Earth will be.

Benefits

  1. Easy to verify and select landing sites.
  2. Simple to identify safe locations by inspecting terrain structures and analyses.
  3. Estimates power and communication potential from Sun and Earth visibility.
  4. Allows choosing the best alternative by comparing multiple sites and durations simultaneously.
  5. Makes data easier to understand through interactive 3D views and heatmaps.
  6. Presents complex space data in plain language.

Objectives and Expected Impact

  1. Mission planning will be faster and more data driven.
  2. A functional analysis platform will be available for future lunar missions.
  3. Scientists, engineers, and researchers will find it easier to make decisions.
  4. Complex geo-data analysis is brought into a simple web interface.

Tools and Technologies Used

  1. Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript.
  2. Frameworks: Next.js, React.
  3. 3D: Three.js, React Three Fiber.
  4. Data Processing: Google Colab (Python).
  5. Data: NASA LOLA DEM, JPL SPICE, JPL Horizons API.
  6. Files: LDEM_80S_80MPP_ADJ, heightmap_1520.f32, heightmap_950.f32, de440.bsp, moon_pa_de440_200625.bpc, pck00011.tpc, naif0012.tls.

Creativity

We made an effort to ensure complex space information is understandable for everyday people. 3D terrain, heatmaps, comparison charts, and visibility overlays have been brought together in one place. Site risk, Sun & Earth positions, and mission efficiency can be viewed side by side. Instead of reading lines of numbers, users can see the entire picture with their own eyes to make decisions.

What Our Team Considered

  1. Safety: Whether the landing site is stable and safe.
  2. Power: How much solar illumination is available at the site.
  3. Communication: How connectivity with Earth will perform.
  4. Terrain Characteristics: Slope, roughness, barriers, and relief.
  5. Mission Planning: Determining which site and date are optimal overall.
  6. Data Reliability: Clearly displaying data sources and limitations.
  7. User Experience: Ensuring information is intuitive, easy to understand, and interactive.
